# Pinned dependency remediation contracts

These are minimal, trusted consumer fixtures for an automated
before / candidate / restored-version contract. They preserve the two dependency
relationships exercised during the 2026-09-21 project experiments. They do **not**
copy the external applications or repeat their builds, HTTP checks, or full scans.
A passing contract establishes only the checks listed below; it does not establish
that every application using these packages is secure or compatible.

## Catalog scope

The CLI defaults to the full shipped `app/data/cve-catalog.json`. Unknown target
assessments still fail with exit code 1. The October 23, 2026 snapshot contains
`CVE-2026-112366` for picomatch through 4.0.7 and `CVE-2026-112307` for sqlparse
through 0.6.0. Their CPE applicability is unsupported, so even the older candidate
versions below cannot currently receive a successful current-catalog verdict.

CI explicitly uses `--catalog-scope historical-fixture` to preserve the original
positive before / candidate / restored regression. `historical-catalog.json`
contains every advisory for the fixture's indexed packages (picomatch, sqlparse,
and Django) from Shipit revision
`b1e0d50d235b0fb6963504e65e459be5b5e9295e`. Its provenance records the original
full catalog SHA-256, upstream CVE/GHSA commits, and packages absent from that
snapshot. The runner checks the fixture file's pinned SHA-256 before any install.
This historical file is test data; production and browser scanners continue to
use the full shipped catalog.

Report version 2 identifies `catalog_scope`, the selected catalog digest, and
historical provenance. In historical mode `fixture_verified: true` applies only
to that historical cycle. A separate `current-catalog-evidence.json` checks the
same installed candidate against the full shipped catalog and records its verdict.
`current_candidate_verified: false` remains explicit when that check is blocked
or unavailable; historical success is not current remediation approval.

The offline tests pin the two October 2026 unknown-applicability records as
negative regression inputs. They also keep the existing missing-inventory,
stale-install, unresolved-range, truncation, and restore controls. The runner does
not require a particular CVE to remain unknown in future catalog snapshots.

Run the probes from a disposable fixture directory, using its installed packages.
The probes may remain in this repository and be invoked by absolute path. Each
prints one JSON object. Functional failures exit nonzero. The sqlparse regression
reports a boolean and exits zero even for the expected vulnerable baseline; the
orchestrator must assert the expected `false / true / false` transition.
`installed_path` identifies the actual dependency loaded by the probe so the
orchestrator can reject imports outside the disposable environment.

## npm: picomatch through Rollup pluginutils

- Consumer: `@rollup/pluginutils` **4.1.2**.
- Before and restored override: `picomatch` **2.3.0**.
- Candidate override: `picomatch` **2.3.2**.
- The baseline lock is lockfile version 3, generated by **npm 11.9.0** with
  `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund`.
  It pins all installed packages with npm registry URLs and integrity hashes.
- Change the override through npm, regenerate the lock through npm, and install
  with `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund`. Never edit lock entries
  manually or run dependency lifecycle scripts.
- Invoke `node /absolute/path/to/npm/consumer.cjs` from the disposable fixture.
  `createRequire()` resolves packages relative to that fixture's `package.json`;
  picomatch is resolved from the actual consumer module.
- Nine assertions cover Svelte / JS / TS inclusion, test / node_modules / Markdown
  / SVG exclusion, and rejection of virtual and non-string module IDs.
  `regression: null` explicitly means there is no independent vulnerability
  reproduction in this npm probe. A finding-count transition is catalog evidence.

Consumer relationship provenance: [`naryal2580/vfapi`](https://github.com/naryal2580/vfapi/tree/f36f177e1a32aa49272f4eb52f8be0af3e8f6bc3).
The earlier experiment exercised the actual `ui` project and its build; this
fixture exercises only `createFilter`. Package provenance is the official
[`@rollup/pluginutils` registry metadata](https://registry.npmjs.org/@rollup%2Fpluginutils/4.1.2)
and [`picomatch` registry metadata](https://registry.npmjs.org/picomatch/2.3.2).

## PyPI: sqlparse through Django

- Consumer: **Django 5.2.10**, with **asgiref 3.11.0**.
- Before and restored dependency: **sqlparse 0.5.5**.
- Candidate dependency: **sqlparse 0.6.0**.
- Supported contract environment: **Linux, CPython 3.12**. Windows requires the
  additional `tzdata` dependency; older Python versions can require additional
  dependencies and are outside this fixture's scope.
- Create a fresh virtual environment for each stage, then use its interpreter:
  `python -m pip install --require-hashes --only-binary=:all: --no-deps -r requirements-before.txt`
  (or `requirements-after.txt`), followed by `python -m pip check`.
- Invoke that interpreter with `/absolute/path/to/pypi/consumer.py`.
  Four functional checks cover parsing two statements, Django SQL splitting with
  an embedded semicolon, comment removal, and a parameterized SQLite query with
  quotes and Unicode. SQLite is in-memory; there are no application routes,
  external services, PostgreSQL paths, or migration tests in this fixture.
- The independent `python-snippet-backslash-escaping` regression formats
  `select '\foo\'` as Python, parses the resulting AST, and checks the assigned
  string with `ast.literal_eval`. It **never executes generated Python**.
  Expected baseline/restored result: `passed: false`, `outcome: "SyntaxError"`;
  expected candidate: `passed: true`, `outcome: "literal_roundtrip"`.
  This exercises [GHSA-3496-9g83-7v6x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3496-9g83-7v6x)
  and its [upstream fix](https://github.com/andialbrecht/sqlparse/commit/53ff44b53e27cff78259acc1af015506fea60f63).
  It does not imply that ordinary Django SQL splitting executes generated Python.

Consumer relationship provenance: [`AikidoSec/firewall-python`, Django ASGI sample](https://github.com/AikidoSec/firewall-python/tree/8cbf271caec9f14c40f266a50955623c8cda2750/sample-apps/django-asgi-uvicorn).
The earlier full-project experiment had ten functional checks; this independent
fixture deliberately has four and does not claim that broader coverage.

Wheel SHA-256 values were obtained from the official PyPI version metadata:

| Package | Wheel | Metadata |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Django 5.2.10 | `django-5.2.10-py3-none-any.whl` | [PyPI JSON](https://pypi.org/pypi/Django/5.2.10/json) |
| asgiref 3.11.0 | `asgiref-3.11.0-py3-none-any.whl` | [PyPI JSON](https://pypi.org/pypi/asgiref/3.11.0/json) |
| sqlparse 0.5.5 | `sqlparse-0.5.5-py3-none-any.whl` | [PyPI JSON](https://pypi.org/pypi/sqlparse/0.5.5/json) |
| sqlparse 0.6.0 | `sqlparse-0.6.0-py3-none-any.whl` | [PyPI JSON](https://pypi.org/pypi/sqlparse/0.6.0/json) |

The corresponding exact hashes are committed in the requirements files. No
source distributions, unpinned dependencies, or optional Django extras are used.
